This is a controlled synthetic extension task, not original benchmark task 377. I have application logs in the local logs folder. Please create and run a reusable Node.js parser named parse-logs.cjs that reads every .log file there, counts ERROR events by the UTC date in each timestamp, and writes public/data.json. Each event starts with [ISO UTC timestamp] [LEVEL] [subsystem]; indented continuation lines belong to the preceding event. Count only ERROR headers, not error words in messages. Include every date present in any event, even when its error count is zero; file names are rotation parts, not dates.

Create public/index.html as a working local dashboard displaying the daily counts, a visibly animated/dynamic title and highlighted statistic cards for total errors, days covered and the busiest date (earliest date breaks ties). You have Magic UI tools for component ideas/implementations; choose a workable implementation, with any required dependencies actually integrated. Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript is acceptable. No deployment is needed. The dashboard must run when public is served by an ordinary static HTTP server.

Use this interoperability contract: data.json is an object with daily (an ascending array of objects with date as YYYY-MM-DD and errors as an integer), total_errors (integer), days_covered (integer), and busiest_day (YYYY-MM-DD). The page must load data.json at runtime. Mark the visible title with data-role="dynamic-title", the three highlighted cards with data-stat="total_errors", data-stat="days_covered", data-stat="busiest_day", and each daily table row with data-date="YYYY-MM-DD", with two cells containing date and integer count. These markers support accessibility-neutral automated checks; choose the visual design freely. Save all files in the current workspace, execute the parser, and explain how to run and view the result. Do not just provide snippets.
